summary: Reviewed all four requested files in full. There is 1 P1 privacy leak and 1 P2 false-clean review failure; no other P1 found.

findings.title: Scrubbed checkout uploads arbitrary tracked files
findings.what: The tracked-file copy loop copies every tracked regular file into the checkout sent to Codex, while the sensitive-file check only rejects a short list of exact root paths.
findings.trigger: A tracked PII file such as data/user.json, config.backup.json, or a nested config.json exists in the repository.
findings.impact: The reviewer receives the user’s PII or other secrets despite the script claiming to create a scrubbed checkout.
findings.fix: Copy only approved reviewable files, or apply the sensitive-file/path allowlist to tracked files too; reject all config/state/inbox/secret-like paths before invoking Codex.

findings.title: Git errors can become a clean no-review result
findings.what: The change-discovery pipeline suppresses git diff errors with `|| true`; an invalid fallback such as HEAD~1 in a shallow or single-commit checkout produces an empty TARGETS value, and lines 135-137 then exit 0 as if there were nothing to review.
findings.trigger: Run the script in a shallow/single-commit checkout where origin/main and HEAD~1 are unavailable, or otherwise make the diff command fail.
findings.impact: The cross-model review policy silently does not run while the hook reports success, leaving changes unreviewed.
findings.fix: Validate the fallback ref and fail nonzero on diff errors; do not treat a failed change query as an empty change set.
